description: Web Forms style: table layout, machine-generated names, plain spans as labels, unusual wording, branch finder and off-screen trap.

Utility-class markup, placeholder-only, autocomplete off, email in a text input; returning/new customer columns, where the new-customer box only starts an account; header search and footer newsletter.
Styled-components style hashed classes, ids with no meaning, labels as adjacent divs, unusual wording, display:none and off-screen autofill traps carrying tempting names.
aria-label only with icons beside the inputs, random names, a maths captcha that really is a text box and a remember-me box.
Tabs with Sign in active and Register in a hidden panel of the same DOM; real labels; both panels have tempting fields.
The secret is a text input masked with CSS, autocomplete off; numeric staff number; station departures box on the same page.
Client-rendered shell: nothing but a spinner at load, the form arrives a second later with React-style ids and controlled inputs; a third-party SSO button.
Attributes lie: a username field named email with an email autocomplete hint, a login password hinted as new; a domain checker in the page.
Old forum header: compact inline form, the word for the username is its pre-filled value cleared on focus, table layout; thread search and quick reply box as noise.
Three-part login for practice software: a site code that is neither credential, then a plain Login and Password. Single-letter names and a language select.
Plain email-first with a labelled email box, then a password panel on the same page; footer search.
First input is torn out of the DOM after a spinner and the value moves to a hidden field; question-style wording, no labels, no names.
Real page navigation between steps: identifier on one page (carried in session storage), password on the next. Customer-number wording and a booking lookup on the first page.
Password box is already in the DOM on step one but collapsed and invisible, then opens on Continue; a quote postcode box nearby.
Email on the parent page; the password step is a same-origin identity iframe loaded after Continue. Site search on the parent.
Three screens: mixed identifier, password, then authenticator code. Field names reused across screens, wording varies on each.
Short form: name, email, password with no confirm box, hashed names, terms checkbox.
Long form, placeholder-only, no names or ids, positional markup; birth date selects and referral code in among the real fields.
Autocomplete hints all wrong (off on the email, current-password on the new one), a terse repeat label, a household select and an off-screen website trap.
Tabs with Create account active and a hidden Sign in panel that has the same-looking fields; a footer newsletter.
Business sign-up built with controlled inputs and React-style ids: company, name, work email, phone, password, confirm.
Rendered late, labels as adjacent divs, show/hide toggle and strength meter on the password, promo code, a free text question, and a hidden trap.
Settings page: profile form above with name, bio and contact email, then a labelled three-field password section.
Reset-link page: no current password, placeholder-only new and repeat, hidden token.
Unusual order: new and repeat first, current password last under a confirmation note. Labels as adjacent divs, no names or ids.
Every autocomplete hint is the wrong way round, generic numbered names, terse Existing/Replacement wording, and a password-hint text box.
Bank security page rendered late: an online-password section and a separate phone-banking PIN section with its own three masked fields.
Well-behaved single code box with a proper label and hint; resend countdown.
Six separate boxes with auto-advance and paste, aria-label per box, no names; header search.
Split three-and-three with a dash between, type tel, dot placeholders, no labels at all: only the heading and sentence say what it is.
Looks like six boxes but is one transparent input over painted cells; hashed name, no autocomplete, wording only in the sentence above.
A masked one-time passcode: type password, label as adjacent div, trust-this-device box and a header search.
Four number-type boxes rendered late with no maxlength; a backup-code form is hidden alongside until asked for.
Estonian sign-in, adjacent spans as labels, no names; bookshop search.
Thai registration form, labels in Thai only, hashed names, no confirm wording in English anywhere.
Hungarian change-password page, generic names, profile nickname field above it.
Arabic right-to-left verification page, one numeric box, a label as adjacent div.
Swahili sign-in, placeholder-only; a Swahili newsletter box at the bottom.
Checkout with live card formatting, single expiry, labelled fields; promo code and order note boxes beside them.
Expiry as two selects, masked CVC, labels as adjacent divs, generic names, cardholder last.
Hosted-fields style: number, expiry and CVC each alone in a separate same-origin iframe injected late; cardholder name on the parent, promo box next to it.
Form-plugin style numbered names, Australian terms, suburb for city, state select, country select, delivery note.
British billing form, placeholder and aria-label only, no names, an address-lookup box above the real fields.
Event listing page embeds its account box in a same-origin iframe; parent has its own search and mailing-list boxes.
Purchase-confirmation challenge in two nested same-origin iframes on a checkout page; code box with a bank wording; gift message box on the parent.
Custom elements: a login component with an open shadow root, and each field its own nested component with its own shadow root holding the label and input.
Holiday-stay landing page with a booking widget; a Log in button injects a dialog with the form. Nothing to offer before the click.
Session-expired native dialog pops up a moment after load over a working page: only the password is asked for, the account shown as text; a table filter behind it.
Recipe search with a big query box, filter sidebar and a sort select; only a link says Sign in.
Standalone mailing-list page with first name and email, autocomplete hints present.
Contact-us form: name, email, phone, subject select, message.
Shopping basket: quantity, promo code that looks like a short code box, a voucher box.
Blog post with a comment form: name, email, website, comment.
Order tracking: an order number and an email, two fields that sit like a login.
Gift card balance check: one long number, no PIN, sloppily hinted as a card number.
Account preferences page with no secrets: display name, public handle, time zone, language, bio, notification boxes; a link leads to the password page.
Developer settings: a webhook URL, a retry limit and a signing secret held in a masked input. Not a login.
Manage-booking lookup: booking reference and surname, shaped exactly like a two-field login, with a label word that invites confusion.
Invite-your-team page while signed in: three colleague email rows with role selects and a note. The addresses are other people's.
Classroom quiz join screen: six single-digit boxes for a game code the teacher shows, plus a nickname. Looks like a split code box, is not account security.
